svg.title: A sudden focal deficit runs the stroke protocol: glucose, NIH Stroke Scale and localization, then a non-contrast CT; no blood means an ischemic stroke (CT angiogram and perfusion, tPA within 4.5 hours, thrombectomy for a proximal large-vessel occlusion with a mismatch) or a TIA (CT, ASA, TIA clinic), both followed by a workup for the cause, secondary prevention chosen by cause, and the risk factors and primary prevention; a deficit that is not a stroke may be a mimic (migraine, Todd's paresis, hypoglycemia, psychogenic); blood means an intracerebral hemorrhage (cause by site, BP under 160/110, hold antithrombotics) or a subarachnoid hemorrhage (vessel imaging, neurosurgery)
